# Psalm 10 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Why do You stand so far away, LORD? Why do You hide when I need You most?

**2** The wicked arrogantly hunt down the poor. Let them be caught in the very traps they set.

**3** The wicked brag about their deepest cravings. The greedy curse and reject the LORD.

**4** The wicked are too proud to seek God. All their thoughts are: 'There is no God.'

**5** They seem to succeed in everything they do. Your laws are far above them, out of sight. They sneer at all their enemies.

**6** They think to themselves, 'Nothing can shake me. I'll always be on top — trouble will never find me.'

**7** Their mouths are full of cursing, lies, and threats. Trouble and evil hide under their tongues.

**8** They lurk in ambush near the villages, killing innocent people in secret, watching for helpless victims.

**9** Like a lion crouching in cover, they wait to pounce on the poor. They catch the helpless and drag them away in nets.

**10** Their victims are crushed; they collapse, overpowered by the strength of the wicked.

**11** The wicked think, 'God isn't paying attention. He has closed His eyes. He'll never notice.'

**12** Rise up, LORD God! Raise Your fist! Don't forget the helpless.

**13** Why do the wicked get away with despising God? They think, 'God will never hold me accountable.'

**14** But You see the trouble and grief they cause. You take note of it and punish it. The helpless put their trust in You. You defend the orphans.

**15** Break the power of the wicked and the evil! Hunt down every last trace of their wickedness.

**16** The LORD is king forever and ever! The godless nations will vanish from His land.

**17** LORD, You have heard the longings of the humble. You will strengthen their hearts. You will listen to their cries,

**18** bringing justice to orphans and the oppressed, so that mere earthly people will terrify them no more.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

- **10:1**: The most honest question in the Psalter: Why does God hide when suffering is greatest? The psalmist doesn't soften the accusation — this is raw faith.

- **10:16-18**: The psalm ends not with an answer to suffering but with a declaration of God's kingship and justice. The tension between v.1 and v.16 is never fully resolved — it's held in faith.

— PNEUMA
